subject: Are reactive elements made "dirty" by changing their display size

messages.author: 4245924341146ca2
messages.subject: Are reactive elements made "dirty" by changing their display size
parts:
I have just begun using Shiny and noticed that if I resize the browser window such that a display element (like a plot) changes size or position, the relevant code block in server.R gets rerun, even though no reactive input in that code block has changed.  It is obvious that such behavior is required in order to enable the redrawing of the output element.  I have no problem with that.  But this situation was not mentioned in the tutorial (great BTW) section on "Execution Scheduling".

My question is this: is it correct to assume that this situation is handled simply (and solely) by setting the invalidation flag of any resized reactiveOutputs followed by a "flush" ?

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Are reactive elements made "dirty" by changing their display size
parts:
Hi Bob, this behavior is specific to plots, and then only if the size of the plot actually changes. One of the reactive inputs that renderPlot uses under the covers is the height and width of the corresponding plotOutput element. So when the size of the plotOutput changes, the changed dimension is sent just as any other changes input would be sent, and then a flush is performed. 

Hope that clears things up.
